summary: EmbeddedGateway (embedded_gateway.jac + embedded_gateway.impl.jac, ~190 lines combined) is a full second Gateway implementation that dispatches in-process via ServiceTransport instead of HTTP. Grepped `EmbeddedGateway` across the whole repo: only its own declaration file, its own impl file, and `jac/jaclang/scale/tests/microservices/test_embedded_gateway.jac` reference it — zero production callers. Confirmed `runtime/orchestrator/orchestrator.jac` (the only place that ever builds a live gateway) always constructs `ProcessGateway` and never imports the planner or checks `plan.gateway_mode`/`GATEWAY_EMBEDDED` (grepped `gateway_mode|GATEWAY_EMBEDDED` in orchestrator.jac: no matches). A docs release note (`docs/docs/community/release_notes/unreleased/jac-scale/6937.refactor.md`) describes this as an intended 'live Gateway (ProcessGateway/EmbeddedGateway)' port selected by the planner, but that wiring was never completed in `orchestrator.jac`, so today the class is reachable only from its own unit test.

The 'read the resource, replace it if it exists, create it on 404' try/except idiom is copy-pasted 47 times in this one file (grepped `except ApiException as e` in monitoring.jac -> 47 matches) across ConfigMaps, Secrets, ServiceAccounts, ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, Deployments and DaemonSets for prometheus/kube-state-metrics/node-exporter/grafana/tempo/loki/alloy. The file already has a generic helper for exactly this pattern, `ensure_service` (line 18), but it's only reused for Services — every other resource kind reimplements the same 6-10 line try/except inline instead of calling a generalized `ensure_resource(read_fn, create_fn, replace_fn, body)` helper.

`admin_get_metrics` serializes the live prometheus_client REGISTRY to text via `generate_latest()` and then re-parses that text back into structured dicts with ~80 lines of hand-rolled regex (`_parse_prometheus_text`, using `metric_line_re`/`label_re`), instead of calling `REGISTRY.collect()`, which prometheus_client (already imported in this same file, re-exported from `_optdeps/prometheus.jac`) provides for free as structured Metric objects with name/type/documentation/samples — no text round-trip needed. Grepped `_parse_prometheus_text|_calculate_metrics_summary` repo-wide: only this file and `tests/misc/test_metrics.jac` (which tests the private parser directly) reference them, confirming the parser is bespoke rather than a required integration point.

The entire 55-line file defines `_transport_response_to_dict`, `_get_http_status`, and `_transport_response_to_json_response`, none of which are declared as abilities in `serve.jac` (unlike every other function in the `server/impl/` directory, which implements a matching declaration) and none of which are called anywhere. The live, actively-used equivalent of this exact conversion already exists as `_convert_transport_response_to_json_response` in `jac/jaclang/scale/jserver/impl/jfast_api.impl.jac` (8 call sites there).
